MINUTES
  MALIBU PLANNING COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  FEBRUARY 21, 2023
  TELECONFERENCES – VARIOUS LOCATIONS
  6:30 P.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Orders N-25-20
and N-29-20 and fully teleconferenced from various locations during the coronavirus
disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Smith called the meeting to order at 6:31p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Dennis Robert Smith, Vice Chair John G. Mazza and Commissioners
  Kraig Hill, and Skylar Peak

  ABSENT: Commissioner Jeffrey D. Jennings

  ALSO PRESENT: Patrick Donegan, Assistant City Attorney; Richard Mollica, Planning
  Director; Jessica Bobbett, Senior Planner; Tyler Eaton, Senior Planner; Fletcher Allen,
  Planning Technician; and Rebecca Evans, Recording Secretary

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Vice Chair Mazza moved and Commissioner Hill seconded a motion to approve
  the agenda continuing Item No. 5.B. to the March 6, 2023, Regular Planning
  Commission meeting.

  The question was called and the motion carried 4-0, Commissioner Jennings absent.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Recording Secretary Evans reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted
  on February 10, 2023.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS
  None.

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS
  None.

ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION / STAFF COMMENTS

  Commissioner Hill requested timely responses to questions posed at Planning
  Commission meetings. He asked for the Planning Commission to tour Santa
  Monica College-Malibu Campus (SMC-MC) and the Sheriff’s substation. He
  suggested that resolutions provided in the agenda packet be watermarked as draft.
  He mentioned the SMC-MC was not dark sky compliant. He noted the vision and
  mission statements from the General Plan were also listed in the Malibu Municipal
  Code as definitions. Commissioner Hill stated the calendar events for Planning
  Commission meetings were listed below community events like knitting and yoga
  and should be listed first. The 18-month moratorium on coastal development
  permits due to COVID would expire soon but perhaps should be further extended
  for Woolsey Fire victims.

  Vice Chair Mazza questioned why the City of Malibu would not have authority
  over the SMC-MC and asked the Planning Director why the Dark Sky Ordinance
  was not already enforced for local gas stations. He stated that the COVID-19
  pandemic no longer impacted development and cited a decrease in the price of
  lumber and other construction materials. Vice Chair Mazza agreed with
  Commissioner Hill that more leeway should be given to fire victims than to
  developers when considering time extensions.

  Commissioner Peak asked staff if there was a way to grant group time extensions
  for those who lost homes in the fire and had to deal with COVID-19 pandemic
  issues as well rather than bringing each to the Commission individually.

  Chair Smith agreed that SMC-MC should be required to comply fully with the Dark
  Sky Ordinance. In response to Commissioner Hill, Chair Smith compared the
  Planning Commission in relation to City Council as similar to AAA baseball in
  comparison to Major League Baseball and suggested that may be the reason for the
  lower level of press coverage. He encouraged the Commission to reach agreement
  on the Accessory Dwelling Unit Ordinance to avoid intervention by California
  Coastal Commission.

  In response to Chair Smith, Vice Chair Mazza asserted that a significant number of
  studies should be provided to the Planning Commission before deliberations on the
  Accessory Dwelling Unit Ordinance.

  Assistant City Attorney Donegan cautioned the Commission that discussion
  regarding the Accessory Dwelling Unit Ordinance should remain limited since the
  item would return for a hearing in the future.
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes of February 21, 2023
  Page 3 of 13
  _________________________

  Planning Director Mollica clarified that the City of Malibu had a planning sphere
  of influence on SMC-MC. However, the State Architect’s office and the State
  issued building permits and conducted inspections during construction. SMC-MC
  had not yet scheduled a final inspection with City staff. The Planning Department
  had provided SMC-MC a copy of the executed Resolution with particular reference
  to the Dark Sky Ordinance conditions of approval to draw their attention to the
  matter.

  In response to Commissioner Hill’s concerns regarding media coverage, Planning
  Director Mollica noted the Malibu Times was aware of the Planning Commission
  meetings and in fact published legal notices with meeting dates and times. In regard
  to a draft watermark on agenda report resolutions, Planning Director Mollica
  confirmed that the City Council did not follow that practice. The City Clerk had
  noted the fact that the resolutions were unsigned indicated that they were draft. The
  City tried to maintain one presentation style so Planning Commission documents
  were handled in compliance with City Council practices.

  Vice Chair Mazza asked if there had been any further follow-up regarding the tower
  next to SMC-MC.

  In response to Vice Chair Mazza, Planning Director Mollica informed that a
  conditional use permit application was submitted by Los Angeles County for
  emergency communications. The City had responded with an incomplete letter and
  asked for responses regarding the structure’s height, lighting and colors. The
  County would need to either comply with the executed resolution or seek an
  amendment.
